pr_title: Fix 'role_name : handler' notation if handler contains role name
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY

Allow handler name to contain role name when using `role_name : handler name` notation to notify handlers containing role name.

Handler names beginning with `role_name : ` will _not_ be callable by their `role_name : handler name`, nor their `role_fqcn : handler name` notation to avoid confusion.  
Not sure if this is truly expected behaviour, since `role_name : role_name : handler name` or `role_fqcn : role_name : handler name` could work just as well, but I didn't want to make this design decision.

I had to refactor the `get_name` method a bit to be able to check if the handler name starts with `role_name : ` or `role_fqcn : `.  
Otherwise the first call with `include_role_fqcn = False` would not check if the role name begins with the fqcn role name and the second call with `include_role_fqcn = True` would not check if the role name begins with the non-fqcn role name, thus allowing the handler name to start with said prefixes.

Fixes #70582 

##### ISSUE TYPE

- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
<!--- Write the short name of the module, plugin, task or feature below -->

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

I've added a test to check if handlers containing the role name are callable through their prefixed aliases.  
I have _not_ been able to figure out how to use integration tests to ensure that handler names beginning with the `role_name : ` or `role_fqcn : ` prefix are properly ignored.

issue_context.title: Cannot notify handler via role_name : handler_name, when the handler name also contains the role name
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/adcdee9bb0031577698246fcfc51f8af63a56a17/lib/ansible/playbook/task.py#L124

##### SUMMARY
Handlers can not be referenced with the `FQCN : handler name` notation if the handler name contains the role name.

Not sure what the reasoning is behind this, but a `httpd` role can't have a `restart httpd` handler name if you want to notify it with `notify: 'httpd : restart httpd'`

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
task handler fqcn

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
```
ansible 2.9.10
  config file = /home/twouters/.ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = ['/home/twouters/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /usr/lib/python3.8/site-packages/ansible
  executable location = /usr/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.8.3 (default, May 17 2020, 18:15:42) [GCC 10.1.0]
```

##### CONFIGURATION
Default configuration

##### OS / ENVIRONMENT
All (N/A)

##### STEPS TO REPRODUCE
```
➜  issues-70582 $ find ./
./
./roles
./roles/test
./roles/test/handlers
./roles/test/handlers/main.yml
./roles/test/tasks
./roles/test/tasks/main.yml
./pb.yml
```

`pb.yml`
```yaml
---

- hosts: localhost
  roles:
    - test
```

`roles/test/tasks/main.yml`
```yaml
---

- name: always trigger handler
  command: /bin/true
  changed_when: True
  notify:
    - 'test : handler 1'

- name: always trigger handler 2
  command: /bin/true
  changed_when: True
  notify:
    - 'test : handler 2 test'
```

`roles/test/handlers/main.yml`
```yaml
---

- name: handler 1
  debug:
    msg: this is handler 1

- name: handler 2 test
  debug:
    msg: this handler is not found
```

##### EXPECTED RESULTS
Two handlers are detected.

##### ACTUAL RESULTS
Only the handler that doesn't contain the role name in its name gets detected

```
➜  issues-70582 $ ansible-playbook pb.yml           
[WARNING]: No inventory was parsed, only implicit localhost is available
[WARNING]: provided hosts list is empty, only localhost is available. Note that the implicit localhost does not
match 'all'

PLAY [localhost] ***********************************************************************************************

TASK [Gathering Facts] *****************************************************************************************
ok: [localhost]

TASK [test : always trigger handler] ***************************************************************************
changed: [localhost]

TASK [test : always trigger handler 2] *************************************************************************
ERROR! The requested handler 'test : handler 2 test' was not found in either the main handlers list nor in the listening handlers list
```

The check in task.py seems overly naive.  It should probably be improved.

Not sure if this is what was supposed to be the purpose? If so, I'd be happy to push a PR

```
if self._role and self.name and not self.name.startswith("%s : " % role_name):
```

review_comments: There are a lot more changes here than I expected from the conversation in issue report.  This is going to require careful review, and potentially unit tests to validate the behavior hasn't fundamentally changed.

yeah, was a bit disappointed about the required changes.  
i could've been less invasive but then it would have become a complete mess :disappointed:

Since self.name is user-defined, is there a benefit to checking for strings in it rather than just always prepending the role name? What is the expected behavior if a handler's name defined at the start of the main play starts with `role_name : ` and a handler name in a role also starts with `role_name : `? I think I'd still expect for the handler in the role to be prefix to be able to distinguish it from the other handler.

Related to that, I'm not sure if it's a bug (though it seems like the intention was to give the user a way to prefer the role's namespace), but this code uses definition order rather than verifying there is not a matching fully qualified handler name before falling back to a less exact candidate. https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/plugins/strategy/__init__.py#L486 So if someone has a handler defined at the start of the play named 'role_name : something' and a handler named 'something' in the role role_name, what should `notify: 'role_name : something'` do inside the role? I don't know, but I think we might want to scope this out and document it to help prevent breakage in the future.
Hm... I think the original reason for the string checking logic was for the callback.

> Since self.name is user-defined, is there a benefit to checking for strings in it rather than just always prepending the role name? What is the expected behavior if a handler's name defined at the start of the main play starts with `role_name : ` and a handler name in a role also starts with `role_name : `? I think I'd still expect for the handler in the role to be prefix to be able to distinguish it from the other handler.

Not sure if I understand correctly, but if a handler has been defined with a duplicate name, the first one defined will be notified.
This is afaik one of the reasons to prefix the handler name with `role_name : `. (Edit: i.e. prefix the handler name when notifying)
So if you want to distinguish the handlers, notify `role_name : ` for the one defined in the play and `role_name : role_name : ` to call the role defined handler. (If the handler name starts with `role_name : ` it becomes a bit awkward, but that seems like designed)

Yeah, that is the current behavior. The precedence of notification is sort of tangential to my thoughts about your change (not suggesting you change that code), but the behavior on devel is different than the original implementation (I'm using 8218591fecf124f3bb8db22030959e235b450f02 as the source of truth for how it was 'supposed' to work), so it just adds another layer to consider. I think this method is overloaded. Before that commit, it looks like get_name was really just used for debugging output and the callback, and then that commit used it for the handler search.

> (If the handler name starts with role_name : it becomes a bit awkward, but that seems like designed)

I think it's ambiguous if it's like designed. My rambling might be entirely wrong, but the more I look at it, the more I don't think https://github.com/ansible/ansible/commit/8218591fecf124f3bb8db22030959e235b450f02#diff-ac960c5e7aa7ed715ac443f64451bff6R108 was supposed to have anything to do with the handler search really; I think it was added just to avoid displaying an additional `role_name : ` for the callback. The string checking seems fragile so maybe callbacks should use a distinct path, and then everything else can just use the one-liner fix `if self._role and self.name:`.

Alright, I think I get what you're trying to say.

This PR was an attempt to try to limit the changes to the then-current design, while allowing the role name to be part of the handler name, as I don't feel comfortable enough with the whole process/codebase to propose other changes without some guidance.  
So feel free to contact me on IRC/matrix if you want to discuss this more. I'll join #ansible-devel right away.
